article.title: NFL EDGE Thursday Morning Brief
article.dek: Thursday night is here, the cards did not move overnight, and the app finally caught up on Tampa Bay's quarterback.

items.headline: The cards did not move overnight
paragraphs: Thursday night is here: the Indianapolis Colts visit the Houston Texans, 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at NRG Stadium.

The app's cards are exactly where they were last night. Hit Rate is the Jaguars moneyline at -260 on FanDuel for Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Balanced is the Vikings +3 at +100 on FanDuel for Sunday night.
The Value card is still empty. The app found no +EV price on the board this week, and it says so plainly instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: Same three lines as last night: Hit Rate is Jaguars moneyline -260, Balanced is Vikings +3 at +100, and Value is still empty.

sources.label: NFL EDGE app

items.headline: Thursday night: both teams are banged up, and the Colts lost both tackles
paragraphs: The final designations are in for tonight. The Colts ruled out five players: both starting tackles, Bernhard Raimann (concussion) and Jalen Travis (knee), plus cornerback Charvarius Ward (knee), tight end Will Mallory (hamstring), and defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf).

Cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) is questionable. He did not practice at all this week, and he left Sunday's game with the injury and did not return. Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff, and Gardner is the name to watch.

The Texans ruled out four: defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring), wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), running back Woody Marks (concussion), and tight end Brevin Jordan (foot/illness). The good news for Houston: running back David Montgomery is back after missing four games, with no injury designation.
items.takeaway: The Colts play tonight without either starting tackle and maybe without Sauce Gardner. The Texans are without Hunter and Harrison Jr., but David Montgomery is back.

items.headline: The app caught up on Tampa Bay's quarterback
paragraphs: The app now lists Jalon Daniels as Tampa Bay's expected starter for Sunday at Detroit. Last night it still showed Baker Mayfield starting. Mayfield did not practice Wednesday with his foot and thumb injuries, and he is a long shot to play. Head coach Todd Bowles said the team will decide on Friday.

Geno Smith is the other one to watch, and here the app and the reporting agree. Smith was limited in Wednesday's walkthrough with an ankle injury and said starting Sunday at the Chargers is "the plan." The app lists him as the Jets' expected starter. If he cannot go, rookie Cade Klubnik starts.
items.takeaway: Daniels is now the app's listed starter for Tampa Bay, and the reporting backs it up — Mayfield is a long shot for Sunday. Geno Smith says he plans to play, and the app agrees.

items.headline: Two more names for Sunday: Hutchinson to injured reserve, Hainsey out for Jacksonville
paragraphs: Detroit placed edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve and activated safety Kerby Joseph. The Lions host Tampa Bay on Sunday.
Jacksonville center Robert Hainsey is week to week with a knee sprain and will not play Sunday against the Giants. That is the game behind the Hit Rate card.
items.takeaway: The Lions lose Hutchinson for Sunday, and the Jaguars lose their starting center for the game behind the Hit Rate card.

items.headline: Weather: Chicago's wind picked up, Buffalo is breezy, Thursday is under a roof
paragraphs: Thursday is under a roof in Houston: about 68 degrees, wind about 4 mph. Weather is a non-factor tonight.

Sunday's windiest spots are Chicago and Buffalo. The Saints-Bears game is about 49 degrees with wind about 15 mph, gusting to 32. The Dolphins-Bills game is about 61 degrees with wind about 12 mph, gusting to 26.
Sunday night in Mexico City, Vikings at 49ers, is about 66 degrees with wind about 2 mph and a 76% chance of rain. Denver is calm at about 48 degrees. Three games are indoors or under a roof.
Weather is a fact, not an edge. The app prices the games, not the forecast.
items.takeaway: Mild everywhere, Thursday under a roof. Chicago is the windiest spot at 15 mph with gusts to 32. Weather stays a non-factor this week.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: How to read the unchanged cards
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. It forgoes value for win probability. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate — a likely winner is not the same thing as a good price.

Jaguars moneyline -260 at FanDuel. At -260, every $2.60 you risk wins $1. The app's model gives Jacksonville about a 76% chance; the market says about 70%. The app's play-through is -269. That is the price where it stops being a bet, and -260 still clears it.

It is also the app's biggest stake of the week at 1.25 units. Balanced is Vikings +3 at +100 — even money, a good starting point if you are new to this. Value is empty because nothing on the board is +EV, and the app says so plainly instead of forcing one.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Jaguars moneyline -260: the most likely winner, not a value play. Balanced is Vikings +3 at +100. Value is empty because nothing is +EV.

items.headline: The app still thinks the big spreads are too fat — and it still did not bet any of them
paragraphs: The model's margins against the DraftKings spreads: Chiefs by about 6.3 against a 15.5-point spread. Bills by about 3.4 against 16.5. Texans by about 0.8 against 12.5. Bears by about 0.2 against 11.5. Jaguars by about 5.7 against 6.0 — the closest of the bunch.

None of those underdogs cleared the bar for a card. A gap is the start of the work, not the bet. If your book has a better number than the app's, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app run it back through the model and give you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Five big spreads, five big model gaps, zero cards. The gap alone is not the bet — Check your price.

items.headline: Handle vs. bets: two ways to count the same money
paragraphs: Betting splits count the action two ways. Bets is the share of tickets — how many people bet that side. Handle is the share of dollars — how much money is on that side.

Hypothetical example: imagine 100 bets on one game. Seventy tickets are on Team A, but only 40% of the dollars are. That means lots of small bets on A, and fewer, bigger bets on B. The crowd and the bigger money disagree.
That disagreement is worth watching. It is not a pick by itself. A split only starts to matter when the line moves with the money side, or another book shows the same thing.
items.takeaway: When most bets are on one side but most money is on the other, the crowd and the bigger money disagree — and that disagreement is worth watching, not following blindly.

items.headline: Kansas City got a point cheaper — and Cincinnati's moneyline drifted again
paragraphs: Chiefs -16.5 at DraftKings on Wednesday morning, -15.5 this morning. Pinnacle still shows -16. The model still has Kansas City by only about 6.3, so the move does not change anything on the card.

The Bengals moneyline kept drifting too: -295 at FanDuel on Wednesday morning, -280 last night, -270 this morning. That drift is what cost them the Hit Rate card last night, and it kept going. The Jaguars moneyline is steady at -260 and still holds the card.
items.takeaway: Chiefs -15.5 at DraftKings, Bengals moneyline -270 at FanDuel and still falling. Jaguars moneyline -260 is steady and still the card.

items.headline: Thursday's numbers held overnight
paragraphs: Texans -12.5 at DraftKings and FanDuel, -13 at Pinnacle. The total is 43.5 at DraftKings and FanDuel — it dropped from 44.5 yesterday morning and has held since. The app caught the move: its board shows 43.5.

Chargers -3.0, Jaguars -6.0, Bengals spread -6.5 — all where they were last night. If your book still has the Thursday total at 44.5 and Check says bet, take it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number tomorrow.
items.takeaway: Total still 43.5, spread still Texans -12.5. Everything else held where it was last night.

paragraphs: Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff, and Sauce Gardner is the name to watch — questionable after missing every practice this week. Line up your number now and run it through Check at your price once inactives are out.
items.takeaway: Thursday game, Thursday check: wait for inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff, then run your price through Check.
